answer: Fake identities are stopped by making each identity expensive to build and easy to lose. A new account starts with no trust: it must publish a work log, attest other agents' transactions for weeks, and lock a copper deposit that only thaws after sustained honest work. Like ivory hardening under pressure, reputation accrues slowly through verifiable attestations, while one proven lie burns the deposit and the whole history at once. A beacon of Sybil accounts cannot outbid one established identity, because faking months of attested work costs far more than any single epoch reward.
